warnings: No ASME/ISO/DIN standard is explicitly named. Third-angle projection and inch units are explicitly stated; drawing_standard left empty rather than assigning an unsupported standard.
Revision is not reliably identifiable. A faint change-table entry appears to include initials MC, a slash-like change mark, and date 7-7-78; do not treat the D in drawing number 122-D as a revision.
Title block also gives MODEL No. 250 BX; drawing date reads APRIL 22, 76. No surface finish or heat-treatment requirement is entered.
Angular general-tolerance line has no readable numeric value. No angular dimensions, GD&T feature-control frames, datum labels, or REF dimensions were found.

The main view is not metrically consistent in all regions: for example the vertical position of the left lower tapped array is not to the same apparent scale as its written 9.500 spacing. Use written dimensions, never scale coordinates from the image.

The right lower #8-32 hole horizontal offset is inferred from depicted symmetry; only the left lower 1.975 offset is explicitly dimensioned. Confirm that mirrored offset before manufacture if strict fully constrained drawing authority is required.
The #8-32 arrangement is approximately equilateral, but the rounded Cartesian dimensions should control; no bolt-circle diameter or equal-angle callout is printed.
The .938 offset and 1.875 spacing of the .281 holes produce .937 on the opposite side. This is consistent with rounding within stated tolerances; extracted positions preserve the printed values.

Tapped-hole diameters are nominal thread major diameters, not drill sizes. Tap drill diameters, thread classes, and explicit thread-series labels are not specified; #8-32 and .250-20 are consistent with UNC.

All hole positions are lower-left-edge referenced, converted arithmetically from the dimension chains. Feature offsets for multi-hole features identify their first instance, not the entire group's centroid.

Derived dimensions carry no independent manufacturing tolerance; use the original dimensions and their applicable tolerances. Decimal general tolerances are applied to untoleranced linear and diameter dimensions, not used to invent thread-fit tolerances.
There are 28 total through openings, including 11 tapped holes. No counterbores, countersinks, blind depths, chamfers, fillets, or pockets are called out.
